title: Udemy Practice Test #2 — full timed, 75 questions (2026-10-28)

groups.A: Service fact or limit not known cold (IOPS math, KMS Region scope, Firehose targets, DB engine facts)
groups.B: Multi-select half right: one pick from a sibling feature that does not do the job
groups.C: Hybrid / migration path: wrong connectivity or migration strategy for the constraint

11.keywords: gp2 3 TB, need +3,000 IOPS per instance, MOST cost-efficient, EBS vs EFS vs io1
11.trap: Changed the right answer (grow gp2) to EFS during review. EFS is shared network storage, slower per op for random I/O and costs more per GB; it adds no IOPS guarantee. Review change had no new evidence.
11.rule: gp2 baseline = 3 IOPS per GiB (max 16,000). +1 TB = +3,000 IOPS; growing gp2 (or moving to gp3) beats io1 on cost.

13.keywords: serverless upload app, multi-Region users, low latency, API Gateway Regional, S3 uploads
13.trap: 🔁 Picked Global Accelerator in front of CloudFront; GA fronts ALB/NLB/EC2/Elastic IP, never CloudFront or S3. Low-latency upload to S3 is S3 Transfer Acceleration.
13.rule: Global users → API Gateway edge-optimized endpoint + S3 Transfer Acceleration for uploads. GA cannot front CloudFront or S3.

19.keywords: on-prem Chef, minimal change to config workflow, less operational overhead, replatform
19.trap: AWS Config audits configuration; it does not run Chef recipes. Dated question: OpsWorks reached end of life in 2024.
19.rule: Keep Chef/Puppet with managed server = OpsWorks (legacy answer). Today: Systems Manager State Manager or self-managed Chef. Config = compliance audit, not config management.

24.keywords: serverless API, slow image loads, 504 Gateway Timeout, DynamoDB fine, find root cause
24.trap: 🔁 (missed on 10-08 too) Picked API Gateway execution logging; it shows the 504 but not where the time goes. X-Ray traces each hop; Lambda CloudWatch Logs show processing time.
24.rule: Latency / timeout root cause across API Gateway → Lambda → S3 = X-Ray + Lambda CloudWatch Logs. Gateway logs only confirm the error.

25.keywords: Lambda best practices, Select THREE, layers, VPC-enabled needs NAT, concurrency alarm
25.trap: Picked 'over-provision the timeout' — AWS advises right-sizing memory and setting timeouts to realistic values, not over-provisioning. Missed that VPC-enabled Lambda needs a NAT gateway for public access.
25.rule: Lambda: layers for shared code; memory drives CPU; VPC Lambda reaches the internet only via NAT; alarm on ConcurrentExecutions.

33.keywords: Redshift KMS-encrypted, copy snapshots to another Region for DR, snapshot copy grant
33.trap: 🔁 Put the copy grant in the source Region with a source key. KMS keys are Regional, so the grant must be for a key in the destination Region; copy is enabled from the source cluster.
33.rule: Redshift cross-Region snapshot of KMS cluster: snapshot copy grant in DESTINATION Region (destination key), enable copy in SOURCE Region.

45.keywords: RDS MySQL vs Aurora MySQL, Multi-AZ, read replica promotion, engine upgrade, Select THREE
45.trap: Swapped the promotion facts: Aurora replicas are failover targets that can become the primary; RDS MySQL read replicas are promoted to a separate standalone instance. Udemy's 'Aurora Multi-AZ is synchronous' is simplified wording (Aurora replicates storage across 3 AZs).
45.rule: RDS read replica → promote = standalone DB (breaks replication). Aurora replica → failover = new primary of the same cluster.

46.keywords: after DDoS, EC2 + RDS, static images, revamp security, Select TWO
46.trap: Picked ASG + WAF in front of the ASG; WAF cannot attach to an ASG or EC2 directly (only CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito). Route 53 adds Shield Standard DNS-layer protection.
46.rule: DDoS revamp = Route 53 + CloudFront (static on S3) + WAF on CloudFront/ALB; Shield Standard is built in. WAF never attaches to EC2/ASG.

54.keywords: fully serverless, no manual capacity, sensor data, DynamoDB auto scaling
54.trap: 🔁 Picked Firehose writing directly to DynamoDB; DynamoDB is not a Firehose destination. Kinesis Data Streams needs shard capacity planning; EC2 pollers are not serverless.
54.rule: Firehose targets: S3, Redshift, OpenSearch, Splunk, HTTP endpoints, Snowflake/Iceberg — not DynamoDB. Serverless + no capacity planning = SQS + Lambda.

59.keywords: gaming leaderboard, in-memory, single-digit ms, high availability, Select TWO
59.trap: Picked plain DynamoDB; it is disk-based (single-digit ms) but not in-memory. In-memory options are DAX and ElastiCache Redis (sorted sets for leaderboards).
59.rule: 'In-memory' in the stem = ElastiCache (Redis sorted sets for leaderboards) or DynamoDB + DAX, not DynamoDB alone.

63.keywords: detect public S3 object, alarm, notify, auto-remediate, Select TWO
63.trap: 🔁 Picked S3 event notifications; they fire on object creation but cannot filter by ACL (public-read). CloudTrail data events + EventBridge pattern on PutObject with public-read can.
63.rule: Detect an API parameter (ACL, encryption flag) = CloudTrail data events + EventBridge rule → SNS → Lambda remediates. S3 event notifications only know event type and key prefix/suffix.

65.keywords: hundreds of PoC PHP/JS/Python apps, little traffic, lowest infra cost, least development effort
65.trap: Picked rewrite to Lambda + DynamoDB; that is a refactor with large dev effort (PHP not native in Lambda). One EC2/Beanstalk per app wastes cost.
65.rule: Many small idle apps, cheap + little effort = containerize and bin-pack on ECS behind one ALB (dynamic port mapping).

67.keywords: multiple on-prem DCs linked by private fiber, no NAT, HA, high bandwidth, multi-Region
67.trap: Changed the right answer (Direct Connect at each DC from different providers) to DX + VPN backup during review. VPN backup is low bandwidth and the single-VGW design is not multi-Region.
67.rule: HA + high bandwidth hybrid = redundant Direct Connect (diverse providers/locations) with failover across DCs. VPN backup only when cost beats bandwidth.

68.keywords: 140 TB monthly, 10 Gbps DX with private VIF, 200 Mbps internet, by Monday, LEAST expensive, S3
68.trap: 🔁 Picked an S3 VPC endpoint over the private VIF; a gateway endpoint is not reachable from on-premises. S3 public endpoints need a public VIF on the same DX (no extra hardware).
68.rule: On-prem → S3 over Direct Connect = public VIF (cheapest, uses existing DX). Private VIF reaches only VPC resources (or an S3 interface endpoint, newer option).
